questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
Best university world wide for my major.
Interesting culture of city.
I wanted to connect with my dads family who I knew quite poorly that lived nearby.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Big difference between studying at a Danish vs. American university. This change was at times frustrating.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The most difficult thing was becoming a citizen of a new country. A lot of paperwork and moving takes up the most of your time. Integrating into the school was easy. Therefor the assistance I needed was more geared towards being a citizen in a new country, which I felt very alone in. I was not really exposed to information regarding these aspects, so I'd say it was not easy to find.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't get any assistance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Orientation grouping was poorly designed. I was grouped with first year college students of the ages 17-18 from other countries. I had a tough time relating to them. Also the orientation week was very weirdly planned, as there were not very many activities. We just walked around  with our group. Then suddenly there were new groups and again we basically just walked around campus.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was difficult to find a good deal. Dorm prices and other things I was exposed to through my institution were well over my budget. I ended up finding out about cooperative housing through some friends. After a week, there was a spot for me and it was way more affordable than anything else.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Go to grocery stores far away from the university town. Better, larger and cheaper.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The coop is in my opinion the only way to go, if you have not secured any grants.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Their website was very easy and informative about tasks and deadlines.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to fill in some stuff online and then when I got there I could pick up my student card the first day of orientation.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Phone, internet, in person help on campus.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the stuff I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Be quick to register for classes so they don't fill up. Often many spots are reserved for students doing a major, so there are only few spots that are open to all. 
When studying at Berkeley, you are often, depending of your major, required to take 13 units. This exceeds the 12 units that translate to 30 acts points. Look for fun and easy classes with no exams that give 1 unit to get to the 13 in total.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A lot of busy work. Very individualistic.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Often very good lectures, and interesting topics. There could be more fun, abstract and challenging papers or exams.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different. I have come to appreciate the freedom, focus on critical thinking and cooperative learning of UCPH more.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Social Psychology
Sociology of Policing
Development and Globalization
Cult Cinema

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Development and Globalization was great. More political economy heavy, even though it is listed as a sociology course but it is very informative and interesting and the professor is GREAT. Very case specific.

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
Phone deals feel like scams
Weekend trips and other stuff just adds up...
Insurance is crazy expensive. DEFINETELY wave the school insurance and get your own for 1/4 of the price.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was part of the rent at my cooperative housing

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Great sport facilities. Again, there is everything you could even think of.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: National parks in the states are amazing. Renting a car and driving is a must. My university had a deal with enterprise car rental which made it very affordable and waved the young driver fee.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy. Annoying bureaucratic interactions.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Live in a coop (cooperative housing).
Do sports or other activities.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: People are more overtly proud. Can seem like bragging to a Dane.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are very open and friendly.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1 Live in a coop! unless you are very freaked out about bad hygiene.
2 Wave SHIP insurance, get your own.
3 Be super disciplined about school. So many papers, if you falls behind once, you might never catch up again.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: USA west coast is built for cars. If you don't have a drivers licence get some friends that do. Driving around and seeing the nature of California should be high priority.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Hanging out with people at the coop and a roadtrip after school was over (and seeing all of my family).

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: School was often unmotivating.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
